walkthrough: Identify the given data: mass $m = 850 \text{ kg}$ and two horizontal forces $1600 \text{ N}$ to the left and $1200 \text{ N}$ to the right.
State the rule: acceleration is caused by the resultant force, $F_{net} = ma$, so opposite forces must be subtracted.
Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force: $F_{net} = 1600 - 1200 = 400 \text{ N}$.
Rearrange for acceleration: $a = F_{net}/m$ and substitute with units: $a = 400/850 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Evaluate and check units: $a = 0.4705... \text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.47 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, which has the correct unit for acceleration. This is option A.
